correctness.rationale: The increment-first-letter boundary rule gives all ordered pairs, so for n <= 9 the length-nine second-substitution blocks over those pairs supply the whole language. Independently, the adjacent differences in the two-block window are D, wildcard, D with D=(0,1,-1,0,1,0,0,1); the wildcard is arbitrary because both block letters range freely. Reversal negates and reverses the differences. Comparing templates for n=3,...,9 uses only the distinguishable constants -1,0,1 modulo q>=3; there are 54,27,15,7,3,1,0 matches respectively, every match fixes every difference, and their integrated normalized signatures reproduce the stated table. The distinct signatures remain distinct modulo every q>=3. Directly reversing them gives 2,1,1,1,1,1,0 palindromic types. Lengths 1 and 2 are elementary; above length 9 any reversible factor would give one at length 9, and the length-eight palindrome makes the barrier sharp. Replay paths: /workspace/branches/audit-2-differences.py (difference-template reconstruction, also independently evaluated) and the exact weighted-disjoint-set enumeration /workspace/branches/7d5b45f9-3fe3-47f9-81d0-ea2796f3c76d/audit_certificate.py (executed and independently corroborated at q=3,4,5). The frozen graph and direct-prefix scripts and captured outputs were inspected, not executed; finite-prefix sampling is not used to establish the universal claim. The result does not cover q=2.

value.rationale: This fixed point is a recognized automatic construction. The exact transition from a sharp length-eight palindrome to absence of every reversible factor at length nine is a strong directional property, beyond just nonclosure under reversal or a finite experimental cutoff. The table distinguishes palindromes from reversible nonpalindromes and its modulus-independent certificate makes it useful across the whole family, not merely at a single small alphabet.
